rationale: This is the first draft for iteration 0, so no race telemetry exists yet and the design rests on contract reasoning rather than measured results. Speed: the course is about 4 to 5 m and must finish within 3 s, so the robot needs an average of roughly 1.5 m/s or more. I set base_speed to 1.5 (PWM about 75 percent) to leave headroom for the average speed to be reached through bends. Sensing: five sensors spaced 2 cm apart across x from -0.04 to +0.04, placed 3 cm ahead of the axle, so the 25 mm tape is always covered by one or two sensors and the signal stays continuous. Sensor size 12 mm is a compromise between sharp response and smooth readings. Weights are linear and antisymmetric (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the signal is proportional to the line offset and its sign matches the steering convention (positive = left). Control: kp 2.5 gives a moderate turn gain (about 875 PWM counts per unit signal at the edge), kd 0.2 damps the response to fast signal changes without amplifying sensor noise much, and ki is 0 to avoid integral windup on the bends. line_loss is last_direction so the robot recovers toward the side it left the tape. Geometry: wheel_track 0.12 m and wheel_radius 0.03 m give a moderate turning radius and a reasonable speed-to-turn ratio, body_width 0.12 m widens the off-track allowance, and mass 0.8 kg keeps inertia low for quick corrections. Expected result: the robot should complete most of the course with few line-loss events and RMS error under about 0.03 m. The first race will show whether the 1.5 speed is too fast (oscillation or off-track on the slalom) or too slow (failure to finish within 3 s), and the observations requested below will indicate which.
